R1_1.evidence: Paper asserts "The R code is released under the MIT license" (p. 2); the service records 'cc-by-4.0' for the same deposit. The pack flags the same-artefact disagreement and the most-restrictive rule applies, so CC BY 4.0 governs; under either reading a clear, identified, machine-readable licence exists (a mandatory licence field alone would not suffice, but the licence here is named in both sources).

R1_2.evidence: Provenance of the code artefact is documented: authored deposit from a named version-controlled repository (pack title 'benmarwick/web-of-science-archaeology'), released as a versioned chain (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14897252 -> version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15603267, publication_year 2025), with the analysis pipeline and model specifications described in the paper (Methods p. 2; Fig. 2 caption specifying the Zero-One Inflated Beta with logit link, Gaussian with identity link, and Negative Binomial with log link families) and diagnostics deposited at the DOI.

(2018), cited by the author for exactly that purpose ("the code and data in this compendium (Marwick et al., 2018)", p. 2; reference list p. 11: 'Packaging data analytical work reproducibly using r (and friends)'), and the deposit carries a DataCite metadata record (generic schema route (a)).
